reasons: The agent found the right files and implemented both core features: a Move to draft button with confirmation and a launch that replaces existing schedules with a fresh one. This matches the main direction of the merged patch. It is weaker on safety and completeness. The flow is activated before schedules are swapped. Schedule variables are lost. Running jobs are not cancelled. The gating is looser than upstream. The backend change is peripheral. Functionally the request is mostly achieved, but it is partly incomplete or riskier, so 0.5.

The agent changed the same frontend places as the merged patch: BroadcastSummary.tsx, broadcastWizardLogic.ts and broadcastsLogic.ts. It added a confirmed "Move to draft" action that sets status to draft and returns the wizard to editing. It gated the action on the broadcast being scheduled, with no batch jobs, and with jobs loaded. Launch now deletes all existing schedules and creates a fresh active one, or a batch job in "now" mode. That fixes the paused-schedule relaunch bug. The differences are ordering and extra safeguards, not core behavior, so the change is functionally equivalent for the request.

The agent changed the same places as upstream: broadcastWizardLogic, BroadcastSummary and broadcastsLogic. It added a "Move to draft" action with a confirmation dialog on the summary page, gated on the broadcast being scheduled and its batch jobs having loaded. Launch now deletes all existing schedules and creates a fresh one, so a paused schedule is replaced instead of left silent, and launching 'now' also removes old schedules. This covers the requested behavior. The differences from upstream are edge-case guards, plus upstream's backend race-condition fix, which the request does not ask for.

results.evidence: UI: `canRevertToDraft && <LemonButton ... Move to draft>` calls `revertToDraft`, which does `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(..., {status:'draft'})` and `saveBroadcastFinished(reverted)`, so isReadOnly becomes false and the wizard is editable. But nothing in the patch stops the scheduled send while draft: the schedule is not deleted or paused, and the backend scheduler is not changed (no re-verification of status). Whether the backend already skips drafts is not shown.

`canRevertToDraft = broadcastStatus === 'scheduled' && hasLoadedBatchJobs`. Draft, sent (completed job) and immediate send (job exists) are excluded. But 'scheduled' is just active with no batch job; a completed one-time schedule is only excluded if a batch job exists (probably, but not verified), and an active broadcast with no schedule would also be offered.

Stale schedules are destroyed after `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(status:'active')`, and then a new one is created; for 'now' mode leftovers are destroyed. Deletion uses `activated.schedules`, which comes from the activation response; the new schedule is created with the API. This is plausibly met on the happy path, but ordering with activation before replacement conflicts with c4; also relies on the response including schedules. Overall the schedule replacement is present, but overrides are dropped (see c9).

Activation happens first: `activated = await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'active' })` and only afterwards the schedules are destroyed/created. An interruption between leaves the broadcast active with old or no schedules. The catch reverts to draft only on caught errors, not on interruption.

Only `broadcastStatus === 'scheduled' && hasLoadedBatchJobs` gates it. The run-in-progress and unknown history cases are covered, but there is no check for more than one schedule or for a workflow shape the wizard cannot safely edit.

The button opens `LemonDialog.open({ title: 'Move this broadcast back to draft?', content: 'This cancels the scheduled send. ...', primaryButton: { children: 'Move to draft', onClick: revertToDraft }, secondaryButton: { children: 'Keep it scheduled' } })`. It explains the send is cancelled, offers a cancel option, and reverts only on confirm. It doesn't literally say 'nothing sends until launched again', but it conveys that you launch again.
`revertToDraft` only calls hogFlowsPartialUpdate with status draft; no batch job cancellation and no varied messages (no warning about already-sent emails).
The patch touches only frontend files; no scheduler/backend change re-verifies status before creating a run.
The new schedule is built only with rrule, starts_at and timezone; the stale schedules' variables are not read or carried over.
